previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with nausea and left flank pain, found to have a left-sided pyelonephritis due to a malfunctioning nephrostomy tube. He had leukocytosis and acute-on-chronic kidney injury. The tube was draining pus, and urine culture grew Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, treated with a 7-day course of meropenem. He underwent two nephrostomy tube exchanges due to occlusion, with the second allowing successful capping. Hyponatremia developed due to excessive fluid intake and CKD, improving with fluid restriction to less than 2 liters daily. Renal function improved, with creatinine decreasing from 4.3 to 2.8. He passed the capping trial, was discharged home, and advised to follow up with urology, nephrology, and primary care, including a repeat CT for a known lung nodule.

On arrival to the floor, patient reports continued pain 
diffusely across his abdomen and flanks. He is not currently 
having any fevers or chills. He denies having any SOB, cough or 
sputum production, chest pain or changes in bowel movements.

Brief Hospital Course:
Summary
========================
___ pmh neurogenic bladder managed with a urostomy (ileoconduit) 
as well as a left kidney obstruction managed with a left 
percutaneous nephrostomy tube, presented with 2 days of 
abdominal fullness, fevers and nephrostomy tube discharge. This 
was consisitent with previous admissions for UTI. He was treated 
with IV antibiotics and improved.  

Acute Issues
==========================
UTI:
Pt had no other complaints to suggest alternative source. CXR 
clear, no new cardiac findings. History of recurrences indicates 
poor source control and possible collection or abscess. 
Daptomycin and meropenem were started empirically, with Ecoli 
growth on urine culture. PICC was placed for ongoing IV 
antibiotic therapy and access. Renal US showed stable 
hydronephrosis from previous exam. ___ did not feel changing 
nephrostomy tube would be helpful but plans to follow as 
outpatient. Urology did not feel there were any additional 
procedures which could benefit the obstruction acutely. 
Therefore patient was continued on antibiotic therapy and 
improved symptomatically. He was discharged in good condition 
with ___ services to complete IV antibiotic regimen at home.

___ on CKD:
On admission the patient was also noted to have ___ on stage IV 
CKD. This was felt to be secondary to dehydration and infection, 
and improved with IVF hydration and adaquate oral fluid intake. 

Hyponatremia
Patient previously had hyponatremia in setting of increased free 
water intake. Patient feels he is helping to clear infection by 
increasing fluid intake. It has been explained that this will 
not be effective. Other potential etiologies include renal 
failure, with ATN on ___. Renal US with stable bilateral 
hydronephrosis. Improved with asking pt not to consume as much 
free water. 

Chronic Issues
===========================
Pain control
Patient with chronic pain problems secondary to T12 paralysis 
and urologic issues. Continued home pain regimen of oxycontin 
and short acting oxycodone/acetaminophen.

HTN
Well controlled, continued home amlodipine.

Seizures
Unknown date last seizure, continued home LeVETiracetam 500 mg 
PO BID.

Transitional Issues
=========================
1. Patient was discharged with Ertapenem for additonal 11 days 
to complete 3 weeks total therapy, per discussion with 
infectious disease. He had a PICC line placed, and will need 
this removed following completion of antibiotic regimen.
2. Follow up appointments were made with his PCP, urology and 
nephrology. Interventional radiology plans to schedule patient 
for nephrostomy tube replacement as outpatient in 2 months. 
3. Patient was set up with home ___ services for antibiotic 
management and disease and symptom management at home. 
4. Patient's recurrent infections indicate poor source control 
and possible continued obstruction despite chronic nephrostomy 
tube. He should be considered for more definitive correction of 
his ureteral stricture with Dr. ___. His nephrostomy tube 
should be left draining to gravity to allow for decompression.
